::: {#fig-ae-codes}

```{python}
#| fig-alt: "A scatter plot of 1,200 points in the plane, coloured by digit from 0 to 9. Points of the same digit cluster together. The clusters of 0, 2 and 6 stand apart, while those of 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9 overlap near the middle."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4))
points = ax.scatter(ae_codes[:, 0], ae_codes[:, 1], c=y_train, cmap="tab10", s=6);
fig.colorbar(points, ax=ax, label="digit");
ax.set_xlabel("code 1");
ax.set_ylabel("code 2");
fig.tight_layout();
plt.show()
```

The [autoencoder](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-autoencoder)'s 2-number codes of the training images.

:::

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
ae_code_mean = ae_codes.mean(dim=0).tolist()
ae_code_sd = ae_codes.std(dim=0).tolist()
print(ae_code_mean, ae_code_sd)
```

The codes have means `r sprintf("%.2f", py$ae_code_mean[[1]])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", py$ae_code_mean[[2]])`,
and standard deviations `r sprintf("%.2f", py$ae_code_sd[[1]])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", py$ae_code_sd[[2]])`.
Images of the same digit get nearby codes,
and some digits, such as 0, 2 and 6, stand apart,
while others, such as 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9, overlap.
Nothing in `ae_loss()` says where the codes should lie,
so these numbers come out of training,
and a different seed would move them.
To make a new image we would have to pick a code to decode,
and the [autoencoder](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-autoencoder) gives no distribution to draw that code from.

:::
